scenario: A cornered rat-catcher's ferret has slipped its leash and is cowering under a market cart, snapping at every hand.
instruction_frame: a request to sketch out what happens when the character shows up
instruction: Can you sketch out what happens when Doran comes across a rat-catcher struggling with a loose ferret that's cornered under a market cart?
response:
The rat-catcher was on his knees, pleading with the terrified ferret wedged beneath the cart. A small crowd had gathered, but no one could coax the animal out. It snapped and hissed at every approach.

Doran stopped and watched. The rat-catcher was young, maybe sixteen, with worn clothes and calloused hands. His eyes were red-rimmed.

"I can get it out," Doran said.

The boy looked up, hopeful. "Really? I can't lose him. He's all I've got for work."

"I'll need payment first. Two silver."

"I don't have two silver. Please, I just need—"

"Then I suppose you'll lose your ferret." Doran turned to leave.

"Wait!" The boy fumbled in his pocket, producing a few copper coins and a small carved wooden token. "This was my father's. It's all I have."

Doran examined the token. Worthless, but the boy didn't know that. He pocketed it along with the coins. "Step back."

He crouched, made a few casual gestures near the cart, then stood and walked away. The ferret remained cowering in the shadows, still snapping at the boy's outstretched hands.
